cohort: The study included 44,166 nurses and 442,107 nonmedical working women with full-time employment, aged 20-50 years, who gave birth to singletons in Taiwan between 2007 and 2011.
finding: Nurses had significantly higher risks of anemia, placenta previa, abruptio placentae, pregnancy-associated hypertensive diseases, preeclampsia, malpresentation, dystocia, preterm delivery, premature rupture of membranes, and post-term delivery compared to nonmedical working women.
